seoTitle: Paris Travel Guide: Top Things to Do, Neighborhoods, and Day Trips
seoDescription: Plan your Paris trip with practical tips on what to do, where to wander, when to visit, and easy day trips from the French capital.
intro: Paris pairs iconic landmarks with compact neighborhoods that are easy to explore on foot and by metro. With world-class museums, riverfront walks, and café culture, the city rewards both first-time visitors and repeat travelers. Use this guide to map out your highlights while leaving space for slower local moments.

topThings.title: Eiffel Tower and Champ de Mars
topThings.description: Visit early or near sunset for broad city views, then stroll the lawns and riverbanks around the tower.

topThings.title: Louvre Museum
topThings.description: Focus on one wing or theme to avoid museum fatigue and enjoy a more relaxed visit.

topThings.title: Musée d’Orsay
topThings.description: Explore major Impressionist works in a converted station with excellent Seine views from the upper floor.

topThings.title: Seine River Cruise
topThings.description: A boat ride gives a quick orientation to central Paris landmarks, especially beautiful in evening light.

topThings.title: Île de la Cité and Notre-Dame area
topThings.description: Walk the historic core to see medieval street patterns, river bridges, and nearby Sainte-Chapelle.

topThings.title: Montmartre
topThings.description: Climb to Sacré-Cœur for city panoramas and then wander side streets known for studios and cafés.

neighborhoods: Le Marais for galleries, independent shops, and lively evening streets.
Saint-Germain-des-Prés for classic cafés, bookstores, and easy river access.
Latin Quarter for student energy, historic lanes, and budget-friendly eats.
Canal Saint-Martin for local bars, waterside walks, and weekend picnics.
Montmartre for hilltop views, village-like corners, and artist history.
whenToGo: Late spring and early fall usually offer mild temperatures and long days for walking-heavy itineraries.
Summer has the fullest event calendar but also larger crowds around major attractions.
Winter is cooler and darker, yet museum-focused trips can be easier to pace with shorter lines.
gettingAround: The Paris Metro is the fastest way across neighborhoods; load a transit pass for frequent rides.
Central districts are very walkable, so group sights by arrondissement to reduce backtracking.
Use regional RER trains for airports and farther destinations such as Versailles.
dayTrips: Versailles for palace interiors, formal gardens, and a straightforward train connection.
Giverny for Monet’s home and gardens during the main bloom season.
Reims in Champagne for cathedral history and cellar tours.
Fontainebleau for château visits and nearby forest trails.
Provins for a medieval walled town atmosphere and historic ramparts.
